Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap delivers smooth, tear-free gameplay and is the sweet spot most gold-tier reporters settle on for demanding MMOs on Deck. FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers GPU headroom while keeping the image reasonably sharp.

profiles.Summary: Once Human is a demanding open-world survival MMO that exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities at native resolution, requiring low settings and FSR upscaling to reach a playable frame rate. It is officially unsupported on Deck but runs under Proton with gold-tier reports, meaning most players get it working with some effort.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports or guides were available — profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and Deck hardware capability. On your first run, check frame rate in an open-world area and a populated town; if performance dips below 30 fps consistently, drop to Max Battery settings and lower View Distance first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 keeps the GPU load low enough for a 30 fps target; GE-Proton is recommended by gold-tier reporters for better MMO launcher compatibility. Expect frame dips in dense player areas.

KnownIssues: Game is marked Unsupported by Valve — launcher or anti-cheat may cause issues on some Proton versions.
As an online-only MMO, a stable internet connection is required; Wi-Fi performance on Deck may cause disconnects.
The game's launcher may require additional Proton configuration or workarounds to bypass.
High VRAM and RAM demands from the MMO environment can cause stuttering in populated areas even at low settings.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With full TDP and GPU clock, the Deck can push toward 60 fps in lighter outdoor areas, but busy towns and combat encounters will pull it back to 40-50 fps; the 60 fps cap prevents uncapped runaway power draw. Texture Quality can be raised to High since the game uses system RAM as VRAM on the Deck's unified memory.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh with a matching frame cap delivers a smooth, judder-free experience that the Deck can sustain in most outdoor zones. Locking to 40 fps at 40 Hz is the sweet spot for this hardware class with an MMO open world.

profiles.Summary: Once Human is an online survival MMO that carries a "Unsupported" Deck rating, largely due to its anti-cheat or launcher requirements, though ProtonDB gold reports suggest many players do get it running with some effort. The Steam Deck OLED's RDNA 2 GPU sits between the minimum and recommended specs, so expect 30–45 fps at reduced settings with upscaling assistance.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended specs versus Deck GPU class (roughly GTX 1050 Ti) and general ProtonDB gold-tier feedback. On first launch, verify the anti-cheat and launcher work under GE-Proton, then check frame rate in the first open outdoor area and adjust the profile accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800 to keep the GPU comfortable within the 8 W TDP. Drop foliage and view distance first if frame rate dips in open areas.

KnownIssues: Game is Steam Deck 'Unsupported' — may require workarounds to launch (e.g. custom Proton version or launch flags).
Online anti-cheat (EasyAntiCheat or similar) may block play or cause disconnects under Proton.
Launcher or account login screens may not render correctly with a controller, requiring temporary keyboard/mouse input.
High VRAM and RAM sharing on the Deck's unified memory can cause stutters in dense open-world areas.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full 15 W TDP with native resolution gives the best visual fidelity the Deck can offer, but expect drops into the low-40s in busy multiplayer zones or during large combat events. If frame rate is unstable, drop Shadow Quality and Foliage Density to Low first.
